title: Four-Cycle Counting in Low-Degeneracy Graph Streams

problem.claim: Approximate the number of four-cycles in arbitrary-order edge streams within a factor of (1+ε).

gap.claim: Existing methods have weaker theoretical bounds, and recent approaches may be less effective on non-bipartite graphs or when four-cycles are unevenly distributed.

contributions.claim: A two-pass sampling-based algorithm uses Õ(κm / √T) space.
A one-pass algorithm remains accurate when four-cycles are not highly concentrated on nodes, edges, or wedges.
For constant-degeneracy graphs, the two-pass algorithm is provably optimal up to lower-order factors by matching the known Ω(m/√T) lower bound.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Both algorithms were evaluated on a variety of real-world graph streams.
The two-pass algorithm consistently outperformed state-of-the-art methods while using substantially less space for a desired accuracy.
The one-pass algorithm was competitive when four-cycles were evenly distributed and matched the theoretical analysis.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies approximate four-cycle counting in arbitrary-order graph edge streams.
It proposes two sampling-based algorithms, including a two-pass space-efficient method and a one-pass method with distributional robustness.
The two-pass method improves theoretical bounds and is optimal for constant-degeneracy graphs up to lower-order factors.
The algorithms are evaluated on real-world streams, with reported advantages for the two-pass method and competitiveness for the one-pass method.
The authors report good performance on non-bipartite graphs such as social networks.

source_observation.claim: The two-pass algorithm achieves a space bound depending on graph degeneracy and four-cycle count, and is reported optimal for constant-degeneracy graphs.

interpretation.claim: Structural graph parameters can enable sharper streaming guarantees than bounds expressed only in terms of graph size.

application.claim: When designing streaming graph algorithms, exploit low-degeneracy structure if it is available or estimable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish comparable guarantees for graphs with nonconstant or unknown degeneracy.

source_observation.claim: The one-pass algorithm is reported accurate when four-cycles are not highly concentrated and competitive when they are evenly distributed.

interpretation.claim: Distributional assumptions can determine whether a one-pass streaming method is effective.

application.claim: Use concentration diagnostics to decide whether a one-pass estimator is suitable for a graph stream.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify performance when four-cycles are highly concentrated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact sampling procedures or accuracy guarantees.
The abstract does not report dataset identities, experimental settings, or numerical results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported empirical findings.
